docs.title: Zyra Programming Language
docs.text:
Zyra is a fast, expressive, statically-typed compiled programming language designed to combine the performance and safety of Rust with the clean simplicity and developer velocity of Go.

{ align=left width=150 }

100% Self-Hosted & Multi-Target

Zyra features a 100% self-hosted compiler written in pure Zyra (zyra.zy, lexer.zy, parser.zy, checker.zy). It compiles down to both native C/Rust binaries and JavaScript ESM modules.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• ⚡ Zero-Overhead Native Executables: Compiles down to native machine code binaries via Rust toolchain.
  • 📦 Algebraic Data Types & Pattern Matching: First-class struct data structures, tagged enum variants, and pattern matching match expressions.
  • 💬 First-Class String Interpolation: Embed variables directly in string literals using "Hello {name}".
  • 🛠 Official VS Code Extension: High-quality syntax highlighting, autocompletion, hover tooltips, and interactive ▶ Run Code Lens buttons.
  • 🌐 Dual Compilation Targets: Targets both standalone native binaries (.exe / ELF) and Node.js / Browser JavaScript ESM modules.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Install Zyra on Windows in one click or on Linux via curl:

WindowsLinux / macOS

Run ZyraSetup.exe standalone installer:

.\ZyraSetup.exe

Install via curl command:

curl -fsSL https://zyra-lang.dev/get | bash

docs.title: Hello World Example
docs.text:
struct User {
  id: Int
  name: String
}

def greet(u: User): String {
  const clean_name = trim(u.name)
  print("Welcome to Zyra, {clean_name}!")
  return clean_name
}

def main(): Int {
  const user = User { id: 1, name: "  Andrea  " }
  const _ = greet(user)
  return 0
}

Run your code natively: 

zyra build main.zy --target rust --native
./main.exe

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Zyra provides native installers and package distribution binaries for Windows, Linux, and macOS.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Download and run the standalone ZyraSetup.exe installer binary:

  1. Download ZyraSetup.exe from the Latest Release.
  2. Double-click ZyraSetup.exe.
  3. The setup tool will:
  4. Copy zyra.exe to %LocalAppData%\Programs\Zyra\bin.
  5. Automatically register Zyra in your Windows Environment %PATH%.
  6. Optionally prompt to install the Zyra VS Code Extension.

Verify installation: 

zyra --help

docs.title: Linux / POSIX Shell
docs.text:
Install via one-line terminal command:

curl -fsSL https://zyra-lang.dev/get | bash

docs.title: Debian / Ubuntu / Zypper Package
docs.text:
Download the .deb package directly: 

sudo dpkg -i zyra_1.0.0_amd64.deb

docs.title: VS Code Extension
docs.text:
Install the official Zyra Programming Language extension from the VS Code Marketplace or install manually via VSIX:

code --install-extension zyra-vscode-1.0.1.vsix

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: Get up and running with your first Zyra program in 2 minutes!

docs.title: 1. Create a Zyra File
docs.text:
Create a file named hello.zy:

def main(): Int {
  const name = "Zyra Developer"
  print("Hello, {name}! Welcome to Zyra.")
  return 0
}

docs.title: 2. Compile & Run Natively
docs.text:
Compile hello.zy into a native standalone binary:

zyra build hello.zy --target rust --native

Run the compiled executable:

WindowsLinux / macOS 
.\hello.exe

./hello

docs.title: 3. Compile to JavaScript ESM
docs.text:
Target Node.js or browser environments:

zyra build hello.zy --target js
node hello.mjs

docs.title: Control Flow & Match
docs.text: Zyra provides if / else conditionals and match pattern expressions.

docs.title: Conditionals
docs.text:
if (x > 10) {
  print("Greater than 10")
} else {
  print("10 or less")
}

docs.title: Pattern Matching (match)
docs.text:
const label = match (status) {
  Active(user) => "Online: {user}"
  Pending => "Pending"
  _ => "Unknown"
}

docs.title: Standard Library
docs.text: Zyra includes built-in primitives for string manipulation, type casting, and file system I/O.

docs.title: len(s: String): Int
docs.text:
Returns string length: 

const length = len("hello world") // 11

docs.title: substr(s: String, start: Int, len: Int): String
docs.text:
Extracts a substring: 

const sub = substr("zyra language", 0, 4) // "zyra"

docs.title: trim(s: String): String
docs.text:
Trims whitespace: 

const clean = trim("  zyra  ") // "zyra"

docs.title: contains(s: String, sub: String): Bool
docs.text:
Substring search: 

const is_found = contains("zyra lang", "zyra") // true

docs.title: file_read(path: String): String
docs.text:
Reads entire file text: 

const content = file_read("config.txt")

docs.title: file_write(path: String, content: String): Bool
docs.text:
Writes text to file: 

const success = file_write("output.txt", "Zyra compiled content")

docs.title: Structs & Enums
docs.text: Zyra features robust algebraic data types including struct product types and tagged enum sum types with pattern matching.

docs.title: Struct Declarations
docs.text:
Declare custom record types with struct:

struct User {
  id: Int
  name: String
  is_admin: Bool
}

docs.title: Instantiation & Access
docs.text:
const u = User { id: 101, name: "Alice", is_admin: true }
print("User ID: {u.id}, Name: {u.name}")

docs.title: Enum Declarations
docs.text:
Enums represent data variants with optional payloads:

enum Status {
  Active(user: String)
  Pending
  Inactive
}

docs.title: Pattern Matching (match)
docs.text:
Deconstruct enum variants cleanly using match expressions:

def inspect_status(s: Status): String {
  const result = match (s) {
    Active(user) => "User {user} is online"
    Pending => "Pending verification"
    Inactive => "User is offline"
  }
  return result
}

docs.title: Variables & Types
docs.text: Zyra is statically typed with type inference.

docs.title: Variable Declarations
docs.text:
• const for immutable bindings: 

    const pi = "3.14159"

  • var for mutable bindings: 

    var count = 0

docs.title: Primitive Types
docs.text:
• Int: 64-bit signed integer (10, -42)
  • String: UTF-8 text string ("hello", 'raw')
  • Bool: Boolean value (true, false)
  • BigInt: Arbitrary precision integer
  • Void: Empty return type

docs.title: Self-Hosted Compiler Architecture
docs.text: The Zyra compiler is 100% self-hosted and written in pure Zyra.

docs.title: Compiler Pipeline
docs.text:
1. lexer.zy: Pure Zyra tokenizer emitting Token structures.
  2. parser.zy: Pure Zyra recursive descent AST parser.
  3. checker.zy: Semantic checker and diagnostic reporter.
  4. zyra.zy: Entry point compiler CLI driver.

docs.title: VS Code Extension
docs.text: Official VS Code Extension for the Zyra Programming Language.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Syntax Highlighting: Keywords, types, strings, string interpolation
  • IntelliSense: Autocompletions for keywords, types, and stdlib
  • Hover Docs: Markdown API signatures and tooltips
  • Code Lens: Interactive ▶ Run Native Zyra Binary button above def main()
